agents: Agents were the product, not a back-office tool. 'Feynman-2' was their AI tutoring engine — an in-workspace tutor agent that explained concepts, generated interactive diagrams, edited the student's writing, referenced both the student's own notes and the web, ran background tasks, and gave feedback mid-session. Mem0 sat inside Feynman-2 to drive per-student 'learner profiles' spanning the whole platform and all its tools, so the tutor could open with things like 'You highlighted the chain rule diagram yesterday — want to apply it to this example?' or 'You stopped at Newton's Second Law. (3) Build-vs-buy on a 3-person team: they estimated 3-4 weeks to build memory infrastructure in-house and integrated Mem0 in 2 days with no changes to core infrastructure. This is the archetypal buyer for agent-memory: a tiny AI-native team whose product is a long-lived personalized agent, where memory is core UX but not core IP, and engineer-weeks are the scarcest resource.
sells_to: Prosumer / B2C — individual students (and peer study groups). Not an enterprise or developer sale. Founders were themselves undergraduate CS/software-engineering students with tutoring and TA backgrounds, selling to their own demographic.
